controls.title: OT Access Control Policy and Procedures
controls.description: Develop, document, and disseminate an access control policy specific to OT environments that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance. Ensure policy accounts for safety-critical and real-time requirements of industrial control systems.
controls.supplemental_guidance: OT access control policies must balance cybersecurity requirements with operational continuity and safety. Emergency bypass procedures should be documented.
assessment_objectives: Verify OT-specific access control policy exists and addresses ICS/SCADA environments

controls.title: OT Account Management
controls.description: Manage OT system accounts including establishing, activating, modifying, reviewing, disabling, and removing accounts. Account management for OT systems must consider shared accounts used for operations, emergency accounts, and accounts required for safety system access.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Many legacy OT systems use shared or role-based accounts. Document compensating controls where individual accountability cannot be achieved.
assessment_objectives: Verify OT accounts are managed with consideration for operational requirements

controls.title: OT Access Enforcement
controls.description: Enforce approved authorizations for logical access to OT systems and components in accordance with applicable access control policies. Access enforcement mechanisms must not interfere with safety-critical functions or real-time process control.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Safety systems may require immediate unrestricted access during emergency conditions. Document conditions under which access controls may be bypassed for safety.
assessment_objectives: Verify access enforcement does not impede safety-critical operations

controls.title: OT Network Segmentation and Information Flow Enforcement
controls.description: Enforce approved authorizations for controlling the flow of information between OT and IT networks, between OT security zones, and between safety and control networks based on defined security policies. Implement network segmentation using firewalls, data diodes, or DMZs.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Network segmentation is a primary defense for OT environments. Use the Purdue model or similar architecture to define zones and conduits.
assessment_objectives: Verify network segmentation between IT and OT zones
Verify data flow controls between security zones

controls.title: OT Remote Access
controls.description: Establish usage restrictions, configuration/connection requirements, and implementation guidance for remote access to OT systems. Remote access to OT environments must employ multi-factor authentication, encrypted communications, and be limited to authorized maintenance activities.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Remote access to OT systems introduces significant risk. Implement jump servers, session recording, and time-limited access where possible.
assessment_objectives: Verify remote access controls for OT environments are implemented and monitored

controls.title: OT Security Awareness and Training
controls.description: Provide OT-specific security awareness training to all OT personnel including operators, engineers, and maintenance staff. Training must cover ICS-specific threats, social engineering targeting OT environments, and safe computing practices for control system environments.
controls.supplemental_guidance: OT personnel may not have traditional IT security backgrounds. Training should emphasize how cyber threats impact physical processes and safety.
assessment_objectives: Verify OT-specific security training is provided to all relevant personnel

controls.title: OT Audit and Accountability Policy
controls.description: Develop audit and accountability policy for OT systems that accounts for limited logging capabilities of legacy devices, bandwidth constraints of control networks, and the need to preserve real-time performance. Define auditable events appropriate for OT environments.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Many OT devices have limited or no native logging capability. Consider passive network monitoring and external log collection where device-level logging is not feasible.
assessment_objectives: Verify OT audit policy addresses constraints of industrial control systems

controls.title: OT Event Logging
controls.description: Identify and log events relevant to OT system security including unauthorized access attempts, configuration changes, firmware updates, safety system activations, process variable anomalies, and communication with unauthorized external systems.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Use passive network monitoring tools (e.g., OT-specific IDS) to supplement device-level logging. Ensure logging does not impact control system performance.
assessment_objectives: Verify OT-relevant events are being captured without impacting control performance

controls.title: OT Security Assessment
controls.description: Assess OT security controls using methods appropriate for industrial environments. Assessments must not disrupt operational processes or safety systems. Use passive scanning, configuration review, and tabletop exercises rather than active penetration testing on live OT systems.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Active scanning and penetration testing can crash legacy OT devices. Test in lab environments or use passive assessment techniques on production systems.
assessment_objectives: Verify assessments use OT-appropriate methods that do not endanger operations

controls.title: OT Configuration Management Policy
controls.description: Establish and maintain configuration management policy for OT systems including PLCs, RTUs, HMIs, DCS controllers, and network infrastructure. Document baseline configurations for all OT components including firmware versions, ladder logic programs, and network settings.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Configuration management for OT must account for vendor-specific tools, proprietary protocols, and the long lifecycle of industrial equipment.
assessment_objectives: Verify OT configuration management policy covers all OT component types

controls.title: OT Baseline Configuration
controls.description: Develop, document, and maintain baseline configurations for OT systems including PLC programs, HMI configurations, controller firmware versions, network device configurations, and safety instrumented system settings.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Maintain backup copies of all PLC programs, HMI projects, and controller configurations in secure offline storage.
assessment_objectives: Verify baseline configurations are documented for all OT components

controls.title: OT Change Control
controls.description: Implement change control processes for OT systems that include impact analysis on safety and operations, testing in representative environments before deployment, rollback procedures, and coordination with operations personnel for maintenance windows.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Changes to safety systems require additional review and validation. Never deploy untested changes to production OT systems.
assessment_objectives: Verify change control processes include safety impact analysis

controls.title: OT Contingency Planning
controls.description: Develop contingency plans for OT systems that address loss of control system availability, safety system failures, and cyber incidents affecting physical processes. Plans must include manual operation procedures, safety shutdown sequences, and recovery priorities.
controls.supplemental_guidance: OT contingency plans must prioritize safety of personnel and environment over system availability. Include procedures for safe manual operation of processes.
assessment_objectives: Verify contingency plans address OT-specific failure scenarios including safety impacts

controls.title: OT System Backup and Recovery
controls.description: Perform and maintain backups of OT system configurations, PLC programs, HMI projects, historian data, and safety system configurations. Store backups in secure offline locations and test recovery procedures regularly.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Backups of OT systems should include all vendor-specific project files needed to rebuild systems from scratch. Test restoration in lab environments.
assessment_objectives: Verify OT system backups are current and recovery procedures are tested

controls.title: OT Identification and Authentication Policy
controls.description: Establish identification and authentication policy for OT systems that addresses the unique challenges of industrial environments including shared operator workstations, devices with limited authentication capabilities, and the need for rapid access during emergencies.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Many legacy OT devices do not support modern authentication. Document compensating controls and plan for authentication upgrades during system modernization.
assessment_objectives: Verify authentication policy addresses OT-specific constraints

controls.title: OT Multi-Factor Authentication
controls.description: Implement multi-factor authentication for remote access to OT systems, for access to safety instrumented systems, and for privileged access to OT network infrastructure. Consider operational constraints when selecting authentication factors.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Biometric or token-based second factors may be preferred in industrial environments where typing complex passwords is impractical.
assessment_objectives: Verify MFA is implemented for remote and privileged OT access

controls.title: OT Incident Response Plan
controls.description: Develop an incident response plan specific to OT/ICS environments that addresses cyber incidents affecting physical processes, coordination between IT and OT teams, safe shutdown procedures, and preservation of forensic evidence from control systems.
controls.supplemental_guidance: OT incident response must prioritize human safety and environmental protection. Establish clear escalation paths between SOC, OT operations, and plant management.
assessment_objectives: Verify OT incident response plan addresses cyber-physical scenarios

controls.title: OT Incident Response Testing
controls.description: Test the OT incident response capability using tabletop exercises, simulations, or functional exercises that include cyber-physical scenarios. Exercises should involve both IT security and OT operations personnel and address scenarios such as ransomware affecting HMIs, unauthorized PLC modifications, and loss of view/control.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Conduct exercises at least annually. Include scenarios based on known ICS threats (e.g., TRITON, Industroyer, PIPEDREAM).
assessment_objectives: Verify OT incident response exercises are conducted and include realistic ICS scenarios

controls.title: OT System Maintenance
controls.description: Perform maintenance on OT systems using approved tools, techniques, and personnel. Control and monitor maintenance activities, especially those performed by vendors or contractors. Verify system integrity after maintenance activities.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Vendor maintenance tools (laptops, USB devices) must be scanned and controlled before connecting to OT networks. Escort and monitor all third-party maintenance personnel.
assessment_objectives: Verify maintenance procedures control vendor access and validate system integrity post-maintenance

controls.title: OT Removable Media Control
controls.description: Control the use of removable media (USB drives, portable hard drives, CDs) in OT environments. Implement technical controls to restrict unauthorized media, scan approved media before use, and maintain logs of media use in OT zones.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Removable media is a primary attack vector for air-gapped OT systems (e.g., Stuxnet). Implement USB device whitelisting and dedicated scanning stations.
assessment_objectives: Verify removable media controls are enforced in OT environments

controls.title: OT Physical Access Control
controls.description: Control physical access to OT systems, control rooms, wiring closets, field devices, and communication infrastructure. Implement layered physical security including perimeter controls, building access, and cabinet/panel locks.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Remote field devices (e.g., RTUs, sensors) require additional physical protection measures due to their distributed locations.
assessment_objectives: Verify physical access controls protect all OT system components including field devices

controls.title: OT Environmental Controls
controls.description: Protect OT systems from environmental hazards including temperature extremes, humidity, electromagnetic interference, and power fluctuations. Implement appropriate HVAC, power conditioning, and EMI shielding for control system equipment.
controls.supplemental_guidance: OT equipment in industrial settings faces environmental stresses not typical of IT data centers. Ensure environmental monitoring and alerting.
assessment_objectives: Verify environmental protections are appropriate for OT equipment locations

controls.title: OT Visitor Control
controls.description: Control and monitor visitor access to OT areas including control rooms, server rooms, and field locations. Require escorts for uncleared personnel and maintain visitor logs for all OT-restricted areas.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Visitors including vendor technicians should not be left unattended in areas with access to OT systems or networks.
assessment_objectives: Verify visitor controls are enforced for all OT-restricted areas

controls.title: OT Risk Assessment
controls.description: Conduct risk assessments of OT systems that consider threats specific to industrial control systems, vulnerabilities in legacy OT components, potential impacts on physical processes and safety, and consequences of loss of view or loss of control scenarios.
controls.supplemental_guidance: OT risk assessments must consider safety impacts, environmental consequences, and economic impacts of process disruption in addition to traditional confidentiality, integrity, and availability.
assessment_objectives: Verify risk assessments address OT-specific threat scenarios and safety impacts

controls.title: OT Vulnerability Management
controls.description: Identify, evaluate, and remediate vulnerabilities in OT systems considering the constraints of patching industrial control systems. Develop compensating controls for vulnerabilities that cannot be immediately patched due to vendor certification requirements or operational availability needs.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Patching OT systems often requires vendor validation, outage windows, and regression testing. Prioritize based on exploitability and network exposure rather than CVSS alone.
assessment_objectives: Verify vulnerability management process accounts for OT patching constraints

controls.title: OT Network Architecture
controls.description: Design and implement OT network architecture using defense-in-depth principles including network segmentation, demilitarized zones between IT and OT, unidirectional gateways for critical data flows, and separation of safety networks from control networks.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Follow ISA/IEC 62443 zone and conduit model. Use data diodes where one-way data flow is sufficient. Minimize connections between IT and OT networks.
assessment_objectives: Verify OT network architecture implements defense-in-depth with appropriate segmentation

controls.title: OT Boundary Protection
controls.description: Monitor and control communications at OT network boundaries including IT/OT interfaces, connections to business networks, remote access points, and connections to third-party systems. Implement application-layer inspection capable of understanding OT protocols.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Use OT-aware firewalls that can inspect industrial protocols (Modbus, DNP3, OPC UA, EtherNet/IP). Block all traffic not explicitly required for operations.
assessment_objectives: Verify boundary protections inspect and filter OT protocol traffic

controls.title: OT Communication Integrity
controls.description: Protect the integrity of OT communications especially for safety-critical commands and setpoint changes. Where supported, implement cryptographic integrity verification for commands sent to controllers and safety systems.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Many legacy OT protocols lack built-in integrity checks. Use network-level protections (VPNs, TLS wrappers) where application-layer security is not available.
assessment_objectives: Verify integrity protections for safety-critical OT communications

controls.title: OT Malware Protection
controls.description: Implement malware protection mechanisms for OT systems where technically feasible. Use application whitelisting on OT workstations and servers. Deploy OT-specific endpoint protection that does not interfere with real-time control processes.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Traditional antivirus may not be suitable for OT systems due to performance impacts. Application whitelisting is often preferred for static OT environments.
assessment_objectives: Verify malware protection is implemented without impacting OT system performance

controls.title: OT Patch Management
controls.description: Establish an OT-specific patch management process that accounts for vendor patch certification requirements, limited maintenance windows, the need for regression testing on representative systems, and compensating controls for systems that cannot be patched.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Never apply patches to production OT systems without vendor validation and testing. Maintain test environments that mirror production for patch validation.
assessment_objectives: Verify OT patch management includes vendor validation and testing before deployment

controls.title: OT Network Monitoring
controls.description: Implement continuous monitoring of OT networks using passive network monitoring tools capable of understanding industrial protocols. Detect anomalous communications, unauthorized devices, configuration changes to controllers, and deviations from normal process behavior.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Use OT-specific network monitoring tools that baseline normal communications and alert on anomalies. Do not use active scanning on OT networks.
assessment_objectives: Verify passive OT network monitoring is deployed and alerting on anomalies

controls.title: OT Supply Chain Risk Management
controls.description: Implement supply chain risk management for OT systems including verification of component authenticity, assessment of vendor cybersecurity practices, and protection against counterfeit or tampered hardware and software components.
controls.supplemental_guidance: OT supply chains are particularly vulnerable due to long equipment lifecycles, specialized vendors, and the consequences of compromised components in safety-critical applications.
assessment_objectives: Verify supply chain protections address OT-specific risks including component authenticity

controls.title: OT Personnel Security
controls.description: Screen personnel with access to OT systems and ensure appropriate background investigations are conducted. Address insider threat risks for personnel with ability to modify safety systems, control logic, or critical process parameters.
controls.supplemental_guidance: Personnel with access to safety instrumented systems or ability to modify PLC logic represent elevated insider threat risk and should receive enhanced screening.
assessment_objectives: Verify personnel screening addresses elevated risks of OT access
